dossier.purpose: Go multi-module monorepo (~350 go.mod files; tag v0.162.0, stable-base v1.1.0) of OpenTelemetry Collector components that are not in the core collector repo: 113 receivers, 47 exporters, 38 processors, 14 connectors, 31 extension directories, shared pkg/ and internal/ libraries, a few CLIs (telemetrygen, opampsupervisor, golden) and a testbed (README.md:40; versions.yaml:4-358). It is a component library; official collector binaries/images are built in a different repo (README.md:42; cmd/otelcontribcol/builder-config.yaml:1-7). Facts against the six questions: (1) OTLP ingest + privacy filter: the OTLP receiver is a core module, not in this repo (builder-config.yaml:154). In-repo filtering pieces are the redaction processor (alpha logs/metrics, beta traces), filter (alpha), transform/attributes/resource (beta). Nothing is specific to Claude Code or Codex; the only GenAI-aware component is a traces-only alpha attribute normalizer for OpenInference/OpenLLMetry spans. (2)/(3) Metrics and events/logs stores: none bundled. Exporters either write local files (file exporter, alpha) or target external servers (ClickHouse, Prometheus remote write, InfluxDB, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Doris, ...). The Prometheus exporter is an in-memory scrape endpoint. (4) Dashboards: none; only a docker-compose example wiring collector -> ClickHouse -> Grafana (logs and traces pipelines only) and a placeholder remote-tap web page. (5) Trace/dataset/experiment store with fixed-workload replay: none (telemetrygen, golden and testbed are test utilities). (6) Local model server / GPU inference: none.

claims.claim: Scope: this is a repository for OpenTelemetry Collector components 'that are not suitable for the core repository of the collector'.

The official core and contrib distributions are available as part of the opentelemetry-collector-releases repository; some components here are in the 'core' distribution (e.g. Jaeger and Prometheus), most only in 'contrib'.
Users are encouraged to build their own custom distributions with the OpenTelemetry Collector Builder, using components from the core repo, this repo, and possibly third-party or internal repos.
Each component has its own support levels, and the stability level is per signal (e.g. Stable for traces but Alpha for metrics and Development for logs).
Stability levels follow the definitions from the core OpenTelemetry Collector repository.
Some features are hidden behind feature gates that can themselves be at different lifecycle stages.
Components are supported by the contrib maintainers group or by specific vendors; actual support will likely be provided by individual contributors, typically a code owner.
Maintainers may at any time downgrade specific components if they are deemed unmaintained or pose a risk to the repository and/or binary distribution.
Governance: 13 listed maintainers; promotion is blocked if more than 25% of maintainers would share an employer.

The README has no install, configuration or usage section: 'Getting Started' links to https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/getting-started/ and 'Security' links to the core repo's security-best-practices document.

install.method: Build the contrib collector from source (contributor workflow; the manifest describes the result as a 'testing only' binary)
Run the official contrib image from GHCR (shown in the telemetrygen README as the receiving collector)
Run the official contrib image from Docker Hub with a writable volume (shown in the file exporter README)
go install telemetrygen (synthetic OTLP generator only, not the collector)
Build the telemetrygen Docker image locally

code.architecture: Go multi-module monorepo (~350 go.mod; root go.mod has no requires and says it is not used for any official binary, go.mod:1-18; go 1.26.0). One module per component under receiver/ (113), exporter/ (47), processor/ (38), connector/ (14), extension/ (31 dirs incl. encoding/, observer/, storage/), plus confmap/provider/, config/configdbauth, scraper/zookeeperscraper, shared libraries in pkg/ (pkg/ottl = OTTL language and functions used by filter/transform; pkg/stanza = log operators; pkg/translator/*; pkg/golden and pkg/pdatatest = test helpers) and internal/. A component = metadata.yaml (status, per-signal stability, codeowners; mdatagen generates the README status table and internal/metadata) + factory.go + config.go + implementation, e.g. processor/redactionprocessor/{factory,config,processor}.go with internal/db and internal/url sanitizers. Binaries are assembled by the Collector Builder from cmd/otelcontribcol/builder-config.yaml (~263 entries: 111 receivers, 49 exporters, 47 extensions, 34 processors, 13 connectors, 9 confmap providers; exporter entries still pin v0.159.0 but make genotelcontribcol appends replace directives to in-tree modules, builder-config.yaml:70-114,290-293; Makefile:474-477). Core-repo modules supply the OTLP receiver, debug/otlp/otlphttp exporters, batch and memory_limiter processors and zpages (builder-config.yaml:17,66-69,117-118,153-154). Ingest-filter-export path available from these parts: otlp receiver (core) -> processors [redaction | filter | transform | attributes | resource | gen_ai_normalizer] -> exporters. Filtering primitives: redaction = allow-list/blocked-key/blocked-value/hash (md5, sha1, sha3, hmac-sha256, hmac-sha512) over resource, scope, span, span-event, log-record and datapoint attributes plus log bodies (processor/redactionprocessor/README.md:4-7,170-173; processor.go:115-331); filter drops spans/span events/metrics/datapoints/logs when any OTTL condition matches (processor/filterprocessor/README.md:4,29-31,54-59; alpha t/m/l, README.md:9); transform (beta t/m/l, README.md:5-7) runs OTTL, whose functions in pkg/ottl/ottlfuncs include delete_key, delete_matching_keys, keep_keys, keep_matching_keys, replace_pattern/replace_all_patterns/replace_match/replace_all_matches, SHA1/SHA256/SHA512/MD5/FNV, truncate_all, limit; attributes processor actions insert/update/upsert/delete/hash(SHA1)/extract/convert (processor/attributesprocessor/README.md:26-37; beta). Sinks and per-signal stability from metadata.yaml: file alpha traces/metrics/logs (exporter/fileexporter/metadata.yaml:7-8); clickhouse beta traces+logs, alpha metrics (clickhouseexporter/metadata.yaml:7-9); influxdb beta all three (:7); prometheus beta metrics, scrape endpoint with 5m expiry (prometheusexporter/metadata.yaml:7; README.md:29); prometheusremotewrite beta metrics (:8); elasticsearch beta traces+logs, development metrics (:7-8); opensearch alpha traces+logs, development metrics (:7-8); doris alpha all three (:8); tinybird alpha all three (:7); cassandra alpha traces+logs, no metrics (:7); awss3 alpha all three (:7); azuredataexplorer beta all three (:7). By name these target external databases/services; only the ClickHouse README was read to confirm an external server endpoint (exporter/clickhouseexporter/README.md:343-348). Receivers otlpjsonfile re-reads whole OTLP JSON files that fileexporter wrote (receiver/otlpjsonfilereceiver/README.md:24-25; exporter/fileexporter/README.md:22). No storage, query, dashboard, experiment/dataset or model-serving module exists in the tree. Other dirs: testbed/ (load, correctness, stability tests), examples/ (couchbase, kubernetes, nomad, logline-filtering, secure-tracing, fault-tolerant-logs-collection), .github/workflows (CI).
code.packaging_and_release: No official release artifacts are built in this repo: builder-config.yaml:1-7 and go.mod:3-9 say official binaries come from opentelemetry-collector-releases (not opened). In-repo release flow: manual workflow 'Automation - Prepare Release' (.github/workflows/prepare-release.yml:1-69) runs .github/workflows/scripts/release-prepare-release.sh (:44-116), which bumps versions.yaml module sets (contrib-base v0.162.0, stable-base v1.1.0, versions.yaml:4-11), updates builder configs and the changelog and opens a '[chore] Prepare release' PR; per-module tags (e.g. processor/redactionprocessor/v0.162.0) and the root tag v0.162.0 all peel to commit ae8c507 (.git/packed-refs:436-437,696-697); Makefile has a push-tags target using multimod (Makefile:281-287). On tag push, build-and-test.yml publish-stable creates a GitHub release with generated notes only (build-and-test.yml:724-787, gh release create at :782); publish-dev builds the scratch-based image (cmd/otelcontribcol/Dockerfile:1-14, base image pinned by digest) and pushes otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib-dev:<sha> and :latest to Docker Hub (build-and-test.yml:689-723); cross-compile builds otelcontribcollite for 14 OS/arch targets (linux 386/amd64/arm/arm64/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x, darwin amd64/arm64, windows 386/amd64/arm64, aix ppc64, solaris amd64) and uploads them only as CI artifacts (build-and-test.yml:601-668). telemetrygen and golden multi-arch images are pushed to ghcr.io/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/{telemetrygen,golden} with dev/latest/<tag> tags (.github/workflows/telemetrygen.yml:58-137; golden.yml:49-132). Makefile has deb/rpm package targets via fpm in Docker (Makefile:628-633). No checksum, signature, SBOM or provenance-attestation step exists in this repo's workflows: a search of .github for cosign|sigstore|slsa|attest|checksum|sbom|syft|gpg found only unrelated text (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/component-graduation.md:54-59, pull_request_template.md:15) and a cache-key sha256sum (build-and-test.yml:466). GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs (e.g. build-and-test.yml:30).

claim_checks.claim: Official core/contrib distributions come from the separate opentelemetry-collector-releases repo, and users can build custom distributions with the OpenTelemetry Collector Builder (README.md:42).
claim_checks.evidence: In-repo statements agree: cmd/otelcontribcol/builder-config.yaml:1-7 ('NOT used to build any official binary'), go.mod:3-9, and builder-config.yaml:12 ('testing only'); the repo itself drives the builder (Makefile:474-483, $(BUILDER) --skip-compilation) and its manifest pulls the OTLP receiver and debug/otlp/otlphttp exporters from core modules (builder-config.yaml:66-69,117-118,153-154). cmd/otelcontribcol contains only builder-config.yaml, Dockerfile, metadata.yaml and .gitignore (no main.go). The releases repo and the builder are outside this tree and were not opened, so the official-artifact half is not checkable here.

claim_checks.claim: Stability is tracked per component and per signal (README.md:44).
claim_checks.evidence: processor/redactionprocessor/metadata.yaml:12-14 (beta traces; alpha logs, metrics) and factory.go:25-27 registers each signal with its own stability constant; exporter/fileexporter/metadata.yaml:7-8 (alpha traces/metrics/logs, development profiles) and factory.go:61-64; exporter/clickhouseexporter/README.md:5-7 (development profiles, alpha metrics, beta traces/logs).

claim_checks.claim: Redaction processor deletes span, log and metric datapoint attributes not on the allow-list and masks values matching the block-list; non-allowed attributes are removed before value checks (processor/redactionprocessor/README.md:4-7).
claim_checks.evidence: processor.go:334-388 processAttrs flags non-allowed keys (shouldRedactKey, :525-532) and skips value checks for them, then removes them (:380-382); blocked values become '****' or a hash (:391-409). The code also covers resource and scope attributes (:145,150,177,182,293,298), span events (:159) and log bodies including nested maps/slices (:186,191-288), which the one-line summary does not state. Default config is the zero value (factory.go:31-33), so with no allowed_keys every non-summary attribute, resource attributes included, is removed (README.md:63-66). Only string values are scanned unless redact_all_types is set (processor.go:357-360). HMAC hashing needs a key of at least 32 bytes (sha256) / 64 bytes (sha512) (config.go:127-147).

claim_checks.claim: For log records whose body is a map, the processor appends audit attributes into the body map itself (processor/redactionprocessor/README.md:213-216).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from README (code preferred): processLogBody receives log.Attributes() (processor.go:186) and addMetaAttrs writes the redaction.body.* keys into that attribute map (processor.go:238-241), for every body type, not into the body map. Also, for non-map/slice bodies an allowed-value match records 'body' and returns, a known TODO tracked as issue 50417 (processor.go:223-229).

claim_checks.claim: GenAI normalizer rewrites attributes on spans from non-OTel GenAI instrumentation into OTel GenAI semantic conventions and applies only to span attributes (processor/genainormalizerprocessor/README.md:15,45-56).
claim_checks.evidence: factory.go:22 registers a traces processor only; processor.go:82-102 iterates span attributes only (:91); built-in sources are only openinference and openllmetry (README.md:19-22) and the default config has no sources (factory.go:28-32). Stability is alpha for traces only (README.md:5). No logs/metrics support and no Claude Code/Codex mapping; 'claude-sonnet-4' appears only as a test value (processor_test.go:596,709,800).

claim_checks.claim: MCP extension 'runs the OpenTelemetry MCP server which enables LLM to efficiently use OpenTelemetry stack' (extension/mcp/README.md:14).
claim_checks.evidence: extension.go:42-58 starts an MCP server over streamable HTTP; internal/mcp/tools/tools.go:31-40 registers eight tools (versions, components, readme, changelog, component schema, schema validation, deprecated fields, RAG) backed by github.com/pavolloffay/opentelemetry-mcp-server/modules/collectorschema (tools.go:15; go.mod:7), i.e. collector docs and config schema; none read telemetry from pipelines or stores. Stability development, no distribution (README.md:5-6). Default endpoint is localhost:8080 (factory.go:29-32) while the README example uses 0.0.0.0:8080 (README.md:21). Start() fails if GetLatestVersion errors (tools.go:26-29; extension.go:47-50); whether that call uses the network depends on the external module, which was not opened.

claim_checks.claim: File exporter writes telemetry to files on disk with rotation and compression; rotation is only enabled when 'rotation:' is specified (exporter/fileexporter/README.md:20-34,88-90).
claim_checks.evidence: config.go:184-206 Unmarshal sets Rotation=nil unless 'rotation' is configured (the default struct sets it, factory.go:68-77); JSON is the default and proto optional (config.go:46-48); zstd only (config.go:132-134); append plus rotation is rejected (config.go:126-128). Facts not prominent in the README: files are created with mode 0644 and file mode is not configurable (factory.go:45,186,198); with no rotation and append false the file is truncated at start (config.go:35-39; factory.go:179-184). Alpha for traces/metrics/logs (metadata.yaml:7-8).

claim_checks.claim: ClickHouse exporter creates the database/tables by default and works with Grafana for visualisation (exporter/clickhouseexporter/README.md:53-62,361,446-449).
claim_checks.evidence: Defaults confirmed in config.go:117-137 (CreateSchema true, AsyncInsert true, TTL 0, tables otel_logs/otel_traces/otel_metrics_*); endpoint is required (config.go:113). The example stack (example/docker-compose.yml:7-90) runs collector + ClickHouse + Grafana with provisioned ClickHouse datasources (datasource.yaml:4-18), but its collector config defines only logs and traces pipelines (otel-collector-config.yml:50-60), so metrics are not exercised, and Grafana runs with anonymous Admin and no login form (grafana.ini:1-7). ClickHouse is an external server, not bundled (README.md:21,343-348).

risks: Scope: no Claude Code/Codex-specific support. The only GenAI-aware component is processor/genainormalizerprocessor - alpha, traces only, built-in mappings for OpenInference/OpenLLMetry only (README.md:5,19-22; factory.go:22). Searching the tree for claude|codex finds only a contributor-policy example (AGENTS.md:50) and test model-name strings (processor_test.go:596). Any allow-lists or redaction patterns for those tools' metrics/events/logs would have to be authored from outside this repo; none are shipped or tested here.

Scope: no store, dashboard, experiment/dataset store or model server in the repo - exporters only. The only server-less sink is fileexporter (alpha; JSON-lines/proto files with no query layer; README says there is 'no guarantee' field names stay stable, exporter/fileexporter/README.md:34) and the Prometheus exporter is an in-memory scrape endpoint with 5m expiry (exporter/prometheusexporter/README.md:16,29). Queryable stores need an external server (ClickHouse: exporter/clickhouseexporter/README.md:21,343-348); its metrics support is alpha (README.md:6) and the bundled Grafana example covers logs/traces only (example/otel-collector-config.yml:50-60). No GPU/LLM-serving code exists (see platforms.gpu).

Security/maturity of the privacy filter: the redaction processor is alpha for logs and metrics, beta for traces (processor/redactionprocessor/README.md:11-12) and its README calls it 'one line of defence rather than the only compliance measure' (README.md:47-49). Behaviours to configure around: zero-value config removes all attributes including resource/scope attributes (factory.go:31-33; processor.go:145,177,293); non-string values are not scanned unless redact_all_types (processor.go:357-360); documented audit attributes for log bodies land in record attributes, not the body (processor.go:238-241 vs README.md:213-216); open TODO on allowed-value handling for non-map bodies (processor.go:223-229). Filter processor is alpha (README.md:9); transform, attributes and resource are beta (their READMEs, lines 5-7).

Security/data handling in fileexporter: output files are created with mode 0644 and file mode is not configurable (exporter/fileexporter/factory.go:45,186,198), so even redacted telemetry is readable by other local users unless the directory is restricted; with no rotation and append false the file is truncated at start (config.go:35-39; factory.go:179-184); the official container image is built on scratch with no writable filesystem by default (README.md:36).

Network exposure in examples and docs: the ClickHouse example binds OTLP gRPC to 0.0.0.0:4317 (exporter/clickhouseexporter/example/otel-collector-config.yml:7; also cmd/telemetrygen/README.md:45), runs Grafana with anonymous Admin and no login form (example/grafana.ini:1-7), uses ClickHouse default/default credentials (example/docker-compose.yml:42-43) and allows an unsigned Grafana plugin (docker-compose.yml:52). Remote-tap and MCP READMEs show 0.0.0.0 endpoints (processor/remotetapprocessor/README.md:41; extension/mcp/README.md:21) while code defaults are loopback (remotetapprocessor/config.go:13; mcp/factory.go:29-32). The core OTLP receiver's own default bind is defined outside this tree and was not verified.

Packaging/supply chain: official release artifacts are not built or signed from this repo (cmd/otelcontribcol/builder-config.yaml:1-7; go.mod:3-9; releases repo not opened). This repo's workflows prepare release PRs/tags, create a notes-only GitHub release (build-and-test.yml:780-786), push a dev image to Docker Hub (:704-722) and telemetrygen/golden images to GHCR (telemetrygen.yml:88-136); no checksum, signature, SBOM or attestation step was found in .github. make otelcontribcol yields a 'testing only' binary (builder-config.yaml:12). The mcp extension depends on an individual maintainer's module pinned to a pseudo-version (extension/mcp/go.mod:7).

Platform coverage is uneven: CI tests run on ubuntu-24.04 (amd64) and ubuntu-24.04-arm (build-and-test.yml:309,443; build-and-test-arm.yml:59); macOS runs only the cgo group (receiver/hostmetricsreceiver) with test binaries built for GOTESTARCH=amd64, on macos-14, and only on push/merge-group or PRs labelled 'Run Darwin' (build-and-test-darwin.yaml:33,59-61,77-78; Makefile:57); darwin/arm64 is otherwise only cross-compiled and not on ordinary PRs (build-and-test.yml:568,602,612-614). WSL2 is not mentioned anywhere. Building from source needs Go 1.26.0 (go.mod:11).

Maintenance and process: all modules except processor/k8sattributesprocessor are v0.x (versions.yaml:4-11); the v1.1.0/v0.162.0 changelog section lists 15 breaking changes, including removed feature gates and config fields (CHANGELOG.md:12-75); one component is flagged unmaintained (receiver/simpleprometheusreceiver/metadata.yaml:11) and others deprecated (exporter/signalfxexporter/metadata.yaml:8; receiver/signalfxreceiver/metadata.yaml:7); support is largely by individual code owners (README.md:60) and several relevant components seek more owners (exporter/fileexporter/README.md:10; receiver/otlpjsonfilereceiver/README.md:17; extension/remotetapextension/README.md:9). There is no SECURITY.md, so vulnerability-reporting instructions are not in this tree.

checks.statement: Build the contrib collector from source (contributor workflow; manifest describes the result as a 'testing only' binary): make otelcontribcol && ./bin/otelcontribcol_<os>_<arch> --config otel-config.yaml
checks.note: CONTRIBUTING.md:13-25 gives exactly `make otelcontribcol` and then `./bin/otelcontribcol_<os>_<arch> --config otel-config.yaml`, with ./bin/otelcontribcol_linux_amd64 as the example at :25. builder-config.yaml:12 reads 'Local OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib binary, testing only.' and :1-7 say the file is not used for any official binary. Makefile:474-483 confirms the output path bin/otelcontribcol_$(GOOS)_$(GOARCH)$(EXTENSION) with CGO_ENABLED=0. The builder is resolved through `go tool` (Makefile.Common:88), so no separate install is needed. The two Docker install commands also match their cited lines word for word (cmd/telemetrygen/README.md:66; exporter/fileexporter/README.md:44).

checks.statement: yes (build; partial tests). darwin/arm64 is cross-compiled in CI on ubuntu runners, but not on ordinary PRs. macOS test runs cover only the cgo group (receiver/hostmetricsreceiver) on macos-14/macos-15 with test binaries built for GOTESTARCH=amd64, and only on push/merge-group or 'Run Darwin'-labelled PRs. The components read declare no unsupported_platforms.
checks.note: Cross-compile: build-and-test.yml:612-614 builds darwin/arm64 on ubuntu-24.04 in the `cross-compile` job. That job is gated to non-PR events or 'ci:full' PRs (:602). Ordinary PRs get only `cross-compile-pr`, which builds linux amd64/arm64 (:568,575-580). Test scope: Makefile:57 sets CGO_MODS := ./receiver/hostmetricsreceiver, which `for-cgo-target` uses (Makefile:374-375). The darwin workflow runs only on push, merge_group or the 'Run Darwin' label (:33,44,72,96). GOTESTARCH: amd64 (:60-61) feeds GOARCH=$(GOTESTARCH) in Makefile.Common:176. None of the 8 named components' metadata.yaml declares unsupported_platforms. Minor imprecision, not material: test binaries are built on macos-14 and macos-15 (:48), but only the macos-14 artifact is uploaded (:65) and run (:77), so tests execute on macos-14 only, as the risks section correctly says. Because the test binaries are amd64, CI never runs a native darwin/arm64 test binary; 'partial tests' means that. The dossier states the GOTESTARCH=amd64 detail itself.

'claude-sonnet-4' test values appear at processor_test.go:596,611,709,716,800,808 and processor_benchmark_test.go:362,429,430,449,452. A case-insensitive whole-word search for claude|codex returns exactly these three files. A plain substring search also hits 21 identifiers named decodeXRayTraceID/decodeXRaySpanID in receiver/awsxrayreceiver/internal/translator/translator{,_test}.go; these contain 'codeX' by accident and are not references to Codex. A further search for anthropic|openai finds only a naming example (genainormalizerprocessor/README.md:165, 'custom.anthropic') and test strings (processor_test.go:597,612; processor_benchmark_test.go:363). No Claude Code or Codex integration exists.

checks.statement: The redaction processor deletes span, log and metric datapoint attributes not on the allow-list and masks values matching the block-list; non-allowed attributes are removed before value checks (verified: yes).
checks.note: README.md:4-7 states this word for word. In processAttrs (processor.go:334-388), a key that shouldRedactKey flags (:525-532; any key not in allowList unless allow_all_keys is set) is queued and skipped with `continue` before any value check (:353-355), then removed (:380-382). Remaining string values are matched against blocked_values (:445-451) and replaced with '****' or a hash (:391-409). The evidence details also check out: resource and scope attributes (:145,150,177,182,293,298), span events (:159), log-body maps and slices (:186,191-288), zero-value default config (factory.go:31-33, so with no allowed_keys every attribute is dropped, per README.md:63-66), non-string values scanned only with redact_all_types (:357-360), and HMAC keys of at least 32/64 bytes (config.go:135-143). One unstated nuance: ignored_keys and ignored_key_patterns skip both checks (:349-351), as documented at README.md:72-80.
